summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted following a syncopal episode at home, resulting in a fall and head strike. Initial CT showed a small subarachnoid hemorrhage, which resolved on repeat imaging the next day. Syncope was attributed to likely vasovagal or hypotensive causes, possibly exacerbated by recent increases in isosorbide mononitrate and transition to extended-release metoprolol, along with poor oral intake and a urinary tract infection. He was found to have a catheter-related MRSA infection, requiring IV vancomycin via a PICC line. The Imdur dose was reduced from 90 mg to 60 mg daily due to hypotensive concerns. He was cleared by physical therapy, remained neurologically stable, and was discharged to an extended care facility for completion of antibiotic therapy. Outpatient follow-up was arranged for meningioma monitoring, renal mass surveillance, and primary care coordination.
